comparison.objective: Compress and pull-lock spring tongs, then place them inside a cutlery-tray compartment; candidate commissions a damper and secures its selected adjustment.
comparison.physical_skill: PR requires squeezing sprung arms, pulling a tab while maintaining closure, transporting, and placing the locked utensil. Candidate requires recessed hex-key alignment, bounded loosening/tightening torque, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and test-cycle iteration.
comparison.success_condition: PR succeeds when the released tongs are locked shut and wholly inside the long compartment for 2 s. Candidate succeeds only after the physical setscrew/collar sequence and two acceptable carriage stops with retained setting.
comparison.reason: Although both include holding against a spring and engaging a lock, their tested mechanisms and outcomes differ materially: utensil state-and-place versus dynamic damper calibration and lock retention. Candidate numeric rebound, overload, and drift limits are missing.
